jobs.description: 1、参与空间智能(含具身、智驾)大模型前沿算法研究,涵盖4D通用表征、多模态感知融合(视觉/触觉/力觉)、空间理解与推理、端到端运动规划、动作生成等模块的数据生成、算法开发、模型训练优化及评测迭代等工作,持续提升大模型空间智能竞争力。 2、开展细粒度4D空间对齐与推理技术研究,在VLM中引入4D空间特征编码网络并对齐到LLM语义空间,同时通过DiT/世界模型等技术提升模型的空间推理能力,实现对4D场景的精细化理解。 3、参与构建大模型的时空间理解与推理能力,实现快慢思考自适应切换,基于CoT压缩与推理加速、高质量CoT生成、强化微调等技术,在保持因果推理能力的同时降低时延,应用于自动驾驶与具身智能。 4、将业界先进VLA, VLN, World Model, Agent, 强化学习, 迁移学习等技术应用于自动驾驶、具身智能领域,实现安全高效的动作生成,提升自动驾驶在复杂场景下的推理、规划和决策能力,以及机器人各类应用的通用技能。 5、协同团队推动算法落地应用与技术竞争力构建:包括大规模数据采集与生成、Sim-to-Real迁移、真机部署等工作,搭建空间智能/具身智能技术平台,确保技术方案领先性与差异化;紧跟业界和学术界空间智能领域最新研究进展,参与业界顶会,将前沿成果融入研发。

Title: AI数据与仿真工程师(双休,需要有全职工作经验)招聘_西湖交互机器科技(杭州)有限公司招聘 - 智联招聘
# AI数据与仿真工程师(双休,需要有全职工作经验) 你的价值,本该更高. 1. 负责机器人及相关业务场景下时序数据、传感器数据与实验数据的全链路治理,完成数据清洗、特征挖掘、统计分析与可视化呈现,为AI算法迭代提供高质量数据支撑。. 2. 参与数据处理核心算法模块的研发落地,覆盖信号滤波、特征提取、异常检测、分类与回归预测等场景,解决多源异构数据的时间同步、对齐融合等技术问题。. 4. 基于Isaac Sim、MuJoCo等主流物理仿真平台,搭建高保真仿真环境与自动化测试工具链,完成仿真场景构建、批量数据生成与仿真结果校验。. 5. 负责数字资产生命周期管理,完成三维模型导入、格式转换、碰撞体设置及基础物理属性配置,保障仿真环境与真实场景的一致性。. 6. 配合算法团队完成数据分析模块、AI训练接口与仿真工具的功能联调、测试验证与问题排查,支撑具身智能算法的快速迭代与落地。. 1. 硕士及以上学历,计算机、人工智能、软件工程、自动化、电子信息等相关专业,欢迎优秀应届毕业生及具备相关项目经验的社会人才投递。. 2. 具备扎实的Python编程能力,能够独立完成数据处理脚本、分析模块及工具的开发工作;熟悉Linux系统基本操作,具备良好的软件调试与问题排查能力。. 3. 熟练使用NumPy、Pandas、Matplotlib等常用数据处理与可视化工具,掌握数据清洗、特征提取、统计分析及时序信号处理的常规方法。. 4. 了解机器学习/深度学习基础理论,熟悉PyTorch、Scikit-learn等框架的基本使用,有相关课程设计、科研项目或实际开发经验者优先。. 5. 对三维模型、数字资产及物理仿真技术有浓厚兴趣,了解USD、URDF、MJCF等常见资产格式,愿意长期深耕仿真工具与平台开发方向。. 6. 满足以下任一条件者优先考虑:有Isaac Sim、MuJoCo等仿真平台实际使用经验;有CAD、Mesh模型处理或数字资产整理经验;有时序数据、传感器数据或多源异构数据融合分析经验;有AI算法、仿真工具或数据分析相关落地项目经验。. ## articles.title: Agentic World Action Models
articles.summary: Recent world action models provide visual foresight and future prediction for robot manipulation, but lack explicit mechanisms for compositional skill reuse. Agentic robotics combines code-based planning and reasoning with reusable skills, but often lacks predictive grounding in physical dynamics. articles.summary: Force-sensitive manipulation requires contact and load information that is not provided explicitly by visual observations. We present CW-WAM, a world action model that jointly predicts video, motion, and contact wrench. Inspired by hybrid motion-force control, it contains a unified interaction module that treats both motion and contact wrench as modeling targets and predicts time-aligned motion-wrench chunks as control references. A pair-causal attention mechanism structures the motion-wrench dependencies, while a long fixed-length wrench memory retains past interaction information. The predicted wrench chunk acts as a force reference for a 20-Hz outer-loop admittance controller within a slow-fast control system that maintains force feedback and smooth motion between model queries. articles.summary: Humanoid fall recovery requires selecting a motion that suits both the surrounding scene and the task. articles.summary: Real-time whole-body humanoid teleoperation remains challenging due to the computational latency introduced by optimization-based retargeting pipelines and future-frame conditioning. articles.summary: Autonomous mobile robots operating in dense crowds and cluttered sites require $360^\circ$ perception to react to surrounding hazards. articles.title: Reconstruction-Augmented Visuomotor Pre-Training of 3D-Grounded Bimanual Dexterity from RGB-Only Human Videos
articles.summary: We present SpatialDex, a framework that learns 3D-grounded bimanual dexterity from RGB-only human videos through reconstruction-augmented visuomotor pre-training. The central idea is to learn human behavior together with its spatial context. articles.title: Joint-Angle Invariance of Jacobian-Based Performance Indices for Serial Robotic Manipulators
articles.summary: This article investigates the joint-angle invariance (JAI) of Jacobian-based performance indices for serial robotic manipulators. We identify kinematic conditions under which representative performance indices, including manipulability, stiffness, and other Jacobian-derived indices, remain independent of the first and last joint angles. This property allows a systematic reduction in the effective configuration-space dimensionality, thereby simplifying the performance evaluation. The utility of JAI is demonstrated through two application scenarios: workspace performance map construction and task layout optimization. Comparative results show that the proposed JAI-based strategy reduces computational effort and storage requirements without compromising the effectiveness.

articles.title: One Policy, Many Styles: Where to Aggregate Preferences for Steerable Humanoid Control?
articles.summary: Modern robotic agents are increasingly expected to support steerable control, where a single policy can adjust its behavioral style at runtime under changing user preferences. Preference-conditioned reinforcement learning provides this interface, but conditioning alone does not ensure that a requested behavior change is strong, does not leak into unrelated behaviors, and does not compromise task performance. Our evaluation combines Preference Reward Responsiveness (PRR) with coverage and utility metrics. This paper presents a posture-aware navigation framework centered on \emph{Adaptive Traversal Tubes} (ATT), \emph{Interval Velocity--Heading} (IVH) control, and a sidestep-enhanced AMP locomotion prior. ATT represents a behavior-feasible corridor width field along a reference path, unifying geometric clearance and social comfort into a continuous signal. IVH maps this width to a continuous frontal-to-sidestep posture schedule and omnidirectional velocity commands. articles.summary: In object goal navigation (ObjectNav), an embodied agent must find a target object (e.g., "find a bed") in a previously unseen environment, relying on spatial commonsense such as object co-occurrence. articles.title: PLaCA: Learning Patch-Level Future Latent Change for Action Generation
articles.summary: Vision-Language-Action (VLA) models generate robot actions from visual observations and language instructions, but effective manipulation also requires anticipating how the environment will change. Existing world-action models explore future image prediction and latent dynamics modeling. However, generating complete future images can be computationally expensive, while highly compressed latent representations may obscure local changes. To address these challenges, we propose PLaCA, a world-to-action framework built around future latent change. PLaCA directly predicts spatially structured patch-level future latent change from the current multimodal input, preserving local information about expected environmental changes. articles.title: JARVIS: From Visual Manuals to Autonomous Robotic Assembly
articles.summary: Visual manuals communicate procedural knowledge through stepwise diagrams, but translating these instructions into reliable long-horizon robotic execution remains challenging. We introduce JARVIS, a method-agnostic benchmark for autonomous visual-manual-guided execution without additional language instructions. JARVIS comprises 236,679 LEGO assembly tasks across 8,987 scenes, with a carefully curated JARVIS-v1 suite of 50 tasks for interactive robotic evaluation. Tasks span varying initial structural complexities and assembly horizons, requiring agents to interpret manuals, ground actions in an evolving workspace, and execute the intended procedure. A structure-aware evaluation protocol captures geometric accuracy, structural relations, construction order, partial progress, and completion. articles.title: EchoNav: Evidential BEV Completion from Historical Observations for Visual Navigation
articles.summary: Visual navigation in cluttered environments requires robots to recover previously observed structure and infer obstacles and free space that remain occluded. We present a framework that combines temporal aggregation and occupancy completion in an evidential bird's-eye-view (BEV) representation predicted from short RGB sequences. A decoder adapts frozen VGGT-Omega features and combines historical residual proposals using cellwise weights and a learned no-update option. The BEV predictor produces a local map in the latest ego frame without depth or camera-pose inputs or explicit geometric warping. The evidential model treats observed free space separately and predicts occupancy with associated confidence across the remaining supported region. We train the predictor on simulated RGB sequences paired with complete and visibility-masked occupancy annotations. articles.title: Embodied Task Agents Can Perform Fine Manipulation through Tactile In-Context Learning
articles.summary: Can embodied task agents use tactile experience to perform fine manipulation without task-specific model training? We investigate this capability through Tactile-ETA, a system that incorporates tactile experience into an embodied task agent through in-context learning. Successful expert demonstrations show how contact changes during manipulation. We pair each recorded robot movement with its camera views and bilateral tactile observations. We keep tactile observations at the start and end of each movement and add two neighboring time points when the tactile images change markedly in between. The agent combines these demonstrations with current vision, tactile observations, and proprioception to select actions through general-purpose robot tools, without updating model parameters. articles.title: Evaluating Social Reasoning in Embodied Vision-Language Models
articles.summary: Foundation models now serve as reasoning layers for robot teams, but it remains unclear whether embodiment-specialized vision-language models (VLMs) preserve the social-reasoning capabilities of general-purpose VLMs. We evaluate Gemini Robotics-ER on SHREC, a benchmark of real human-robot social interactions, and compare it with published general-purpose VLM baselines. Robotics-ER outperforms GPT-4o-mini on error/competence detection but performs worse on detailed social-attribute judgments; adding a visual frame helps one task while hurting the other. These results suggest embodiment-specialized models may perform differently on social judgments that can be read more directly from observable interaction cues versus those requiring more inference about a person's internal state. Because the comparison spans model families, these differences cannot be attributed to embodiment specialization alone. articles.title: HATCH: Hardware-Attested Task Chains for Verifiable Manipulation
articles.summary: Capability claims in robot manipulation are unverifiable, and existing leaderboards are each closed, simulated, or gameable. We propose HATCH, a robot escape room: an openly specified, physically replicable, sensor-scored, and unrehearsable benchmark. Tasks span five skill categories at three difficulty levels and are chained so that the sensor confirming one task's completion unlocks the next, turning a room into a single long-horizon evaluation. Success is confirmed by instrumentation rather than human judgment, scoring is embodiment-agnostic, and object placements are randomized by a run-day seed. Entrants submit attested self-runs (uncut video, sensor logs, and the seed), with occasional organized events for calibration. Task specifications, build guide, bill of materials, and scoring rubrics are released under an open license.

articles.title: Towards Autonomous Bricklaying Using Boston Dynamics Spot
articles.summary: Mobile legged robots offer unique advantages for on-site construction, including the ability to traverse unstructured terrain, climb stairs, and operate independently between spatially separated work zones. This paper presents a proof-of-concept system for autonomous brick stacking using a Boston Dynamics Spot quadrupedal robot equipped with a manipulator arm. The system operates between a supply area and an assembly area, using AprilTag fiducials for localization and autowalk missions for navigation. Target brick positions and orientations are specified in CAD software and exported directly for robotic execution. We evaluate placement accuracy through ten repeated assemblies of a curved four-layer wall comprising 14 wooden bricks. articles.summary: World models enable embodied agents to anticipate action consequences, yet jointly modeling locomotion and manipulation across diverse embodiments remains challenging due to heterogeneous action spaces and limited multimodal supervision. We present Ropedia W0, the first egocentric loco-manipulation world foundation model spanning humans and robots with diverse embodiments. We curate Xp-Data, comprising 10k hours of egocentric human data and 3k hours of robot data with unified multimodal annotations and systematic quality control. A unified kinematic representation encodes locomotion through camera poses and manipulation through projected skeletons, with robot skeletons combining embodiment-specific forward kinematics with extensive manual keypoint annotation and correction. articles.summary: Multimodal reasoning provides robotic foundation models with predictive context needed for reliable action generation. To bridge this gap, we introduce PhysWord, a reasoning-before-acting foundation model built on Physical Words, which use atomic action verbs as shared semantic anchors for continuous representations of physical dynamics. Specifically, PhysWord predicts upcoming atomic action words and directly aligns their contextual hidden states with latent targets derived from the corresponding future observations. articles.summary: Reinforcement learning enables mobile robots to make fast and scalable navigation decisions in constrained human-shared environments. articles.summary: In this paper, we systematically investigate the mechanisms, scaling behavior, and generalization of physical Recursive self-improvement. Different VLMs are evaluated on 18 manipulation tasks under a fixed interaction budget. articles.summary: Recent advances in multimodal models have enabled GPT-6 Astra to perform robotic manipulation through in-context learning. Yet contact-rich control and tactile perception are often regarded as strengths of specialist policies, leaving open whether Astra can directly understand and use tactile observations. We provide, to our knowledge, the first demonstration that Astra directly interprets vision-based tactile images and uses their contact cues for manipulation. articles.summary: This paper presents the hardware implementation of a quadratic program-based controller on Harpy: thruster-assisted bipedal robot to perform thruster-assisted trotting. articles.title: HandsOn: A Large-Scale Simulation Benchmark for Generalizable Dexterous Manipulation
articles.summary: General-purpose manipulation requires reliable behavior across embodiments, objects, and task demands. We introduce HandsOn, a composable simulation platform and benchmark for cross-embodiment dexterous manipulation. It supports five robotic arms, six dexterous hands, and approximately 200 rigid, articulated, and deformable assets in randomized scenes. The benchmark pairs 18,000 curated human demonstrations with 66 human-verified tasks: Core-50 supports demonstration-based learning and execution tests, while Transfer-16 evaluates asset and relation transfer, skill composition, and deformable manipulation without target-task training demonstrations. Qualitative real-robot rollouts illustrate sim-to-real transfer. articles.summary: Robotic manipulation in agricultural environments remains challenging due to variations in plant geometry, occlusion, and camera viewpoints. Pretrained vision-language-action (VLA) and generalist robot policies offer a promising approach to addressing these challenges by learning manipulation behaviors from multimodal observations and language instructions. However, adapting these policies to agricultural tasks requires domain-specific demonstrations, which are costly and time-consuming to collect on physical robots. articles.title: RoboValue: A Fine-Grained Sim-and-Real Benchmark for Unified Evaluation of Robotic Value Models
articles.summary: Robotic value models assess task execution from visual observations and instructions, providing feedback for policy learning and execution monitoring. However, existing evaluations cover only selected aspects of execution understanding, leaving the reliability of value feedback insufficiently tested. We introduce RoboValue, a fine-grained sim-and-real benchmark for unified evaluation of robotic value models. articles.summary: Humanoid robots hold great promise as general-purpose agents in human-centered environments, yet adapting generalist vision-language-action (VLA) policies to real-world humanoid loco-manipulation remains challenging. Unlike fixed-base or wheeled manipulators, humanoids must coordinate locomotion, posture, gaze, and dual-arm manipulation over a high-dimensional whole-body action space, where inaccurate base or waist motions can easily induce unstable and aggressive upper-body compensation. articles.summary: Vision-and-language navigation (VLN) relies on retaining and using relevant observations. Yet growing histories introduce redundancy, and retained information may remain underused. We introduce ReInsBench, a diagnostic benchmark that examines history utilization through controlled continuation trials. Its results show that history-review reinstruction can recover navigation failures using the existing task context. Motivated by this finding, we propose ReInsVLN, a training-free framework supporting memory construction and utilization in frozen navigators. articles.title: Learn the Task, Not the Schedule: Reducing Spurious Cross-Arm Coupling in Bimanual Imitation Learning
articles.summary: A bimanual demonstration specifies both what the robot should do and one particular schedule for when each arm should act. Standard imitation learning does not distinguish task-required cross-arm constraints from incidental scheduling choices, and may therefore exploit opposite-arm progress as a shortcut cue, creating spurious cross-arm coupling even where relative timing is irrelevant for the current task phase. We introduce Constraint-preserving Temporal Recombination (CTR), a training-time data intervention that preserves recorded arm-local sensorimotor content while retiming the corresponding segments to realize admissible schedules that preserve task-required cross-arm constraints. We use CTR to train Diffusion Policy, Action Chunking with Transformers, and $π_{0.5}$, and evaluate them on four simulated and four real-robot tasks. Across six real-robot bimanual progress-state initializations, CTR raises worst-state success from 56% for the strongest non-CTR schedule mixture to 76%.

articles.title: SPAR: Structural Pruning and Action Recovery for Vision-Language-Action Models
articles.summary: The limited onboard computing resources of robots make the inference demands of vision-language-action (VLA) models costly to accommodate. Reducing these demands through aggressive compression, however, can degrade manipulation performance beyond what supervised fine-tuning alone recovers. articles.summary: Human-collected robot manipulation data often mix successful behavior with retries, pauses, recoveries, and failures.
